impact:
src/ccusage.ts:36 emits `'<cmd>' not found. Install Node.js (node + npx), or set CCUSAGE_CMD to your ccusage command …` whenever the configured command cannot be spawned. VERIFIED: this is a byte-parity port of usage.py:117, so it is frozen-oracle text, not an oversight.

Why it is wrong rather than merely dated: the branch is reachable ONLY when the user set CCUSAGE_CMD to something that does not exist (without CCUSAGE_CMD the exe is process.execPath, which always exists). In exactly that situation installing npx fixes nothing — spendbar has no npx fallback at all. So the advice is guaranteed-useless precisely where it appears.

GATES T-007 (publish). Not because the wording is fatal on its own, but because publishing sends the npm page and the binary out together, and they contradict each other: the page says there is no npx fallback while the binary tells you to go install npx. Once published, both are permanent for that version.

Interim mitigation landed in T-023: README's ccusage section carries a short "Known wording bug" note saying the wording is inherited verbatim from the Python tool, that installing npx is NOT the remedy, and to fix or unset CCUSAGE_CMD. That stops the package page from contradicting the binary, but does not fix the binary.

Resolution options for T-007, in preference order:
1. Sanction the divergence: reword the diagnostic, add a numbered ALLOWLIST entry justifying it, and add the parity-case + unit coverage that entry requires. This is the clean fix and the reason the ALLOWLIST exists.
2. Ship 0.1.0 with the README note and reword in 0.2.0 — acceptable only as a deliberate, recorded choice.

Do NOT change the text without the ALLOWLIST entry and tests: the string is currently byte-matched against the oracle by the parity suite, so an unsanctioned edit fails 266-case parity rather than silently drifting.
title: Frozen ENOENT diagnostic advises installing npx, which is never the remedy — gates T-007
